Constructions and their induced maps

A reusable mathematical construction retains an object, its action on maps, and the data needed for the next construction.
Our route: directed dependency → dependent Hom → whole homology → a nonzero connecting map.
The current main book supplies the mathematics. The RHPL overview supplies the computational perspective.

Directed families and transport

E:K⟶U,U=CatcartE:K\longrightarrow U,\qquad U=\mathsf{Cat}_{\mathrm{cart}}E:K⟶U,U=Catcart​
A fibre E[x] is a category. An arrow f:x→y supplies transport E[f]:E[x]→E[y], together with the declared higher action.
(x,u)→(f,a)(y,v),a:E[f](u)⟶v(x,u)\xrightarrow{(f,a)}(y,v),\qquad a:E[f](u)\longrightarrow v(x,u)(f,a)​(y,v),a:E[f](u)⟶v
Current convention: strict functors, with the specified lax transformations. The Cartesian coefficient does not make every base comparison invertible.

Emdash · computational mathematicsThe dependent-Hom ladder

The dependent Hom

homd⁡E(x,u)[y][v][f]=Hom⁡E[y](E[f](u),v)\operatorname{homd}_E(x,u)[y][v][f]=\operatorname{Hom}_{E[y]}(E[f](u),v)homdE​(x,u)[y][v][f]=HomE[y]​(E[f](u),v)
Five parameters: x and y in K; u in E[x]; v in E[y]; and f:x→y. The family E remains fixed in this discussion.
First transport u along f. Then compare that transported object with v inside E[y]. An object of this Hom is a possible fibre component a.
The central issue is coherent variation in all five parameters. The leaf formula alone does not specify the whole higher construction.

The coefficient category

P(I)=T([I,T(U)]),Hom⁡Q(A,B)=Cart⁡(A,P(B))P(I)=T([I,T(U)]),\qquad\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal Q}(A,B)=\operatorname{Cart}(A,P(B))P(I)=T([I,T(U)]),HomQ​(A,B)=Cart(A,P(B))
Ix=Hom⁡K(x,−),SE(x)=Transf⁡K,Q(ιE,ιIx)I_x=\operatorname{Hom}_K(x,-),\qquad S_E(x)=\operatorname{Transf}_{K,\mathcal Q}(\iota E,\iota I_x)Ix​=HomK​(x,−),SE​(x)=TransfK,Q​(ιE,ιIx​)
U supplies admitted fibres. P retains a varying presheaf classifier. The coefficient category supplies represented maps, mates and their selected composition.
Unfolding a fixed Hom in the coefficient category preserves that composition. It does not replace the whole y-transformation by an ordinary diagonal family.

Source and target variance

Source variation uses represented mates. Its shifted index is covariant on arrows and reverses the next transformation level, accounting for C₂(K).
Target variation uses represented maps and a lax comparison. The outer fibrewise opposite compensates the source shift; the root is strict across x.
{f1,f2}⟶{∗},qf1=k=qf2\{f_1,f_2\}\longrightarrow\{*\},\qquad qf_1=k=qf_2{f1​,f2​}⟶{∗},qf1​=k=qf2​
The ordinary negative-section picture clarifies polarity. Its direct higher extension is not the current construction; the selected solution retains the whole coefficient-valued transformation.

Native inputs for homology

Cn+1→dn+1Cn→dnCn−1,dndn+1=0C_{n+1}\xrightarrow{d_{n+1}}C_n\xrightarrow{d_n}C_{n-1},\qquad d_n d_{n+1}=0Cn+1​dn+1​​Cn​dn​​Cn−1​,dn​dn+1​=0
The native input keeps the incoming object, outgoing arrow diagram and one whole diagram map. Its morphisms retain compatible maps of these data.
The internal Hom and dependent-Hom structure supports this input category. Whole universal operations can then act on both its objects and its maps.
For homological results, work in the stated ordinary additive setting with chosen whole kernel/cokernel structures. Row exactness and normality enter at the later connecting/exactness stages.

A nonsplit polynomial example

R=Q[x],S=R/(x)R=\mathbb Q[x],\qquad S=R/(x)R=Q[x],S=R/(x)
A∙=B∙=(R→xR),D∙=(S→0S)A_\bullet=B_\bullet=(R\xrightarrow{x}R),\qquad D_\bullet=(S\xrightarrow{0}S)A∙​=B∙​=(Rx​R),D∙​=(S0​S)
0⟶R→xR⟶S⟶00\longrightarrow R\xrightarrow{x}R\longrightarrow S\longrightarrow00⟶Rx​R⟶S⟶0
The inclusion multiplies by x in both degrees; the projection is the quotient map. If s:S→R is R-linear, then x·s(1̄)=0, hence s=0. It cannot split the quotient.

Computation, interpretation and proof

Computed: selected presentations, matrices, coefficient witnesses and equations. These data remain available for later calculations.
Supplied: the whole model, its normality, row semantics and agreements with the selected complete arrows.
Derived: canonical image-to-kernel comparison inverses and exactness certificates for the actual displayed diagram. No new output-exactness assumption is added.
A raw calculation, an interpretation contract and a conditional formal derivation have different roles. The current interface preserves those distinctions.

Scope and further reading

The Homd ladder retains coherent parameter action. Whole universal operations retain that action through homology and the connecting transformation.
The nonsplit example makes the computational distinction visible: a nonzero connecting map, relation-aware quotient maps, and selected data reused by a conditional exactness certificate.
Current scope: the stated ordinary/additive structures and supplied model interpretations. General higher models, unbounded complexes and global metatheory are not established by these examples.
Read: current book §2.7.1 and Chapter 31; Appendix G; the November 6 Homd communication draft. RHPL supplies the computational perspective.

A calculation of homology is often only
the beginning of a mathematical task.
We may next need the map induced
by a chain map, or a comparison
as the complex varies.
This presentation asks how those
operations can remain part of the
construction itself, rather than being
reconstructed from isolated output
objects.
We follow that question through the
current Emdash book.
The first part explains the dependent
hom and its observation ladder.
The second builds homology and a
connecting transformation from whole
universal operations.
A nonsplit polynomial example will
make the payoff concrete:
the connecting map is an identity, even
though no linear splitting is available.
Let K be a category of parameters
and let E be a directed family.
An object x determines a fibre category.
A base arrow f supplies a functor
between fibres,
so an object u in the source
fibre can be transported to E of
f applied to u in the target
fibre.
An arrow in the total category must
remember that transport.
It consists of the base arrow f
and a fibre arrow from the transported
object to v.
The two components are typed together.
This is the ordinary picture that
motivates the dependent hom formula we
will use throughout the first part.
The current foundations specify the
profiles more carefully than that
informal picture.
Public functors are strict, while
transformations retain their stated lax
comparisons.
Families take values in the Cartesian
coefficient universe.
These choices control which higher
actions exist and in which direction
their comparison cells go.
The dependent hom has a familiar value
once all of its parameters are fixed.
Start with u in the fibre over
x,
transport it along f, and take the
hom from that transported object to v
in the fibre over y.
An object of this hom is precisely
a possible fibre component of a total
arrow.
There are five parameters in this
expression: the two base objects, the two
fibre objects, and the arrow between the
base objects.
The displayed value explains one
observation.
A useful internal construction must
also say how the result varies when
any of these parameters varies,
including the appropriate higher action.
The distinction is consequential.
Two proposals could agree on this final
formula while assigning different
directions to a higher comparison.
We therefore want a whole construction
whose successive observations recover
the formula, while retaining the
variation that later categorical
constructions will consume.
Consider a second base arrow q, from
y to z.
It changes both the target object and
the outgoing base arrow: v becomes its
transport along q, and f becomes q
after f.
Applying the transport functor to a
gives the forward comparison displayed
on the slide.
This direction is the one supplied by
transport.
Requesting a comparison in the reverse
direction would demand extra structure,
and may fail even in an ordinary
example.
A point formula that suppresses all
action can hide this issue, which is
why variance belongs in the
mathematical interface.
In the whole construction, the
comparison lives in the profunctor
coefficient category.
The simple operation sending a to its
transport is recovered on represented
inputs.
It explains the comparison without
identifying every element of the larger
composite with such a simple input, or
asserting a complete higher coend
model.
Three pieces of notation organize the
whole construction.
U is the admitted coefficient for
families.
P of an index category retains the
presheaf- like values together with
their higher mapping profile.
The coefficient category, written with a
calligraphic Q, has the Cartesian hom
categories shown in the first formula.
Now fix x and consider its
representable family.
Send both that family and E through
the represented inclusion into the
coefficient category.
The transformations between those two
diagrams form S sub E of x.
This is where the entire dependence on
y is retained as one categorical object.
The type of one component can be
unfolded into an ordinary functor
category.
But this does not change the
composition used by the whole
transformation.
In particular, it does not manufacture a
covariant ordinary family from diagonal
point values.
The coefficient category keeps the two
moving endpoints connected through its
own operations.
The ladder starts with a whole strict
root.
At a chosen base object x, its
component is a functor from the fibre
into the opposite of the whole
transformation category.
Fixing u gives an object of that
transformation category.
We have already retained all of the
y dependence before selecting a
particular y.
Next observe its component at y.
What remains is a functor from the
target fibre into the index category P.
Choosing v gives an object of P,
which has a fixed- object presheaf view
on the reversed hom category of base
arrows.
These are successive observations of
the same original construction.
Finally apply that presheaf at f.
We recover the target- fibre hom
displayed earlier.
The ladder has therefore carried much
more than the endpoint formula:
it retains the transformations,
functors, and presheaf action that
survive at each intermediate stage,
where further constructions may need
them.
The source- contravariant view at x can
also be written as a functor from
the opposite of E of x into
S sub E of x.
Opposites preserve object carriers but
change higher directions.
Neither that observation nor the last
leaf identifies all the intermediate
categories with a list of pointwise
values.
The two base variables do not use
identical actions.
